# ConstantMap { #timetoalign.ConstantMap }

```python
ConstantMap(
    value,
    source_unit=None,
    target_unit=None,
    uid=None,
    name=None,
    seed=None,
)
```

A ConversionMap that returns a constant value for any input.

Used to associate a fixed label (e.g., a filename) with every coordinate
on a timeline. Typically used inside a `timetoalign.CombinationMap` to
pair a numeric conversion (pixels to seconds) with a string label
(source image filename).

The constant value can be of any type, though strings are the most
common use case; a manifest holds a number or a string. The map has no
source or target unit by default; a numeric constant on a target unit is
written as that unit writes numbers. With a target unit the constant must
be a number or a string: any other value is refused at construction.

## Attributes {.doc-section .doc-section-attributes}

| Name   | Type                | Description                                  |
|--------|---------------------|----------------------------------------------|
| value  | [Any](`typing.Any`) | The constant value returned for every input. |

## Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> cmap = ConstantMap(value="page1.jpeg", name="filename")
>>> cmap(42.0)
'page1.jpeg'
>>> cmap(np.array([1.0, 2.0, 3.0]))
array(['page1.jpeg', 'page1.jpeg', 'page1.jpeg'], dtype=object)
```

### inverse { #timetoalign.ConstantMap.inverse }

```python
ConstantMap.inverse()
```

ConstantMap cannot be inverted.

| Name   | Type                                         | Description                                                 |
|--------|----------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [NotImplementedError](`NotImplementedError`) | Always, as a constant function has no well-defined inverse. |
